findings.title: Materials: 52-point lens gap, 108% growth bet
findings.body: Materials' trailing P/E sits at the 84th percentile while its forward multiple is at the 32nd, a 52-point split that is the widest in the table. The market is underwriting 108 percent earnings growth, which would be an extraordinary repricing if it materializes.

findings.title: Health Care: forward percentile at absolute ceiling
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E has reached the 100th percentile of its five-year range, a level no other sector touches. The 45 percent compression from trailing to forward implies analysts expect an 80 percent earnings surge, a bet that leaves no room for disappointment.

findings.title: Real Estate: rich percentile jump, flat lenses
findings.body: Real Estate's forward percentile surged 37 points in a month to 46, yet its forward and trailing P/Es are nearly identical at 36.83 and 36.44. The re-rating is purely sentiment-driven, with implied earnings growth of just 1 percent decline, so the multiple is not backed by any fundamental improvement.
